subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should the repository accept these updated third-party action revisions in token-, registry-, security-, and API-key-bearing workflows after an exact-head rebase and direct Codex source review?
rationale: Immutable pins reduce supply-chain drift, but the changed action code executes inside privileged workflows and the repository explicitly routes several touched files through security ownership.

options.title: Approve after full verification
options.body: Rebase, inspect the exact Codex and upstream action changes, obtain security-owner approval, and merge when the exact head is green.

options.title: Split sensitive action families
options.body: Land routine setup and maintenance action bumps separately from Codex, token-minting, CodeQL, and release-action updates to narrow review and rollback scope.

options.title: Defer the refresh
options.body: Keep current pins until the sensitive action revisions can be reviewed and validated without the present source-inspection gap.

recommendation.title: Approve after full verification
recommendation.body: Rebase, inspect the exact Codex and upstream action changes, obtain security-owner approval, and merge when the exact head is green.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest individual history signal spans the Codex agent workflow and broader Actions/Docker modernization, with security CODEOWNERS still required for protected files.
